newsitem.title: USA: US corp bonds end lower, tobacco and MFS post gains.
newsitem.headline: US corp bonds end lower, tobacco and MFS post gains.

text.p: U.S. tobacco debt rebounded and MFS Communications Co notes jumped on merger news in what was otherwise a weak U.S. corporate bond market, dealers said.

Spreads for Philip Morris Cos Inc's debt due 2006 closed five basis points tighter at 90 bid, 85 offer. Lower-rated RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp 10-year debt ended at 265 bid, 255 offer compared with Friday's 275 bid, 270 offer.
Tobacco debt rode a severe downward trajectory last week until an Indiana jury late on Friday ruled in favor of four tobacco companies in a suit filed by a family of a smoker who died of lung cancer.

In the verdict, the Marion County Superior Court found for RJ Reynolds Tobacco Co, Liggett Group Inc, Philip Morris and The American Tobacco Co, a unit of Brown & Williamson, which is owned by B.A.T. Industries Plc.
Traders said the verdict was a breath of life for tobacco debt, which has been burnt since early August when a Florida jury awarded $750,000 in damages to a longtime smoker in a similar lawsuit.
News of a stock swap merger with WorldCom boosted MFS Communications Co Inc's $1.6 billion in outstanding debt and preferred stock, junk traders said.

MFS 8-7/8 percent senior discount notes due 2006 were last quoted up six on the bid side at a 68-1/4 bid, 69 offer. The 9-3/8 percent senior discount notes due 2004 went out six higher also, at 81-3/4 bid, 83 offer.
Both Standard & Poor's and Moody's Investors Service Inc said they may raise their respective B/B1 ratings on the senior discount notes.

The stock swap merger with WorldCom Inc will create a telecommunications giant with market capitalization topping $23 billion, analysts said. WorldCom redeemed all of its outstanding rated debt last on August 16, 1996.

Other active issues included American Standard, unchanged at 89-5/8 bid, 90 offer, Stratosphere Corp, up 1/2 to 82 bid, 84 offer, the new Omni paper gained to 100-3/4 bid, 101-1/8 offer, and Grand Union 12.0 percent notes dropped 1/2 to 99 bid, par offer.

Moody's on Monday affirmed Omnipoint's B2 rating. The affirmation of rating came despite Omnipoint's $100 million increase in the size of its debt issue, Moody's said, offsetting higher indebtedness against potential benefits of reducing future funding needs to develop its wireless network and near-term dependence on secured debt.
Also, Sprint Spectrum's $273 million tranche of 10-year senior discount notes were bid at 56, compared with last Tuesday's original level of 54.687.
Traders spotted no markets for Farm Fresh Inc's 12.25 percent senior notes. Heightened cash flow concerns spurred a six point drop to 79 bid late last week, traders said.
High-grade corporates fell along with U.S. Treasuries on followthrough from Friday's decline and ahead of the auction of $31.25 billion in fresh government supply this week, analysts said.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond closed down 18/32 to 96-28/32 to yield 7.00 percent while the Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 28.85 to end at 5693.89.
No new issues priced in the primary market which has effectively shutdown until after the upcoming Labor Day holiday next Monday, syndicate officials said.
